title: Admission surface optimizer and attention-prefetch policy for continuous batching
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Background:
Redwood's continuous batching stack achieves good average throughput but customers report occasional tail-latency spikes during sustained mixed workloads (short/long tokens, variety of models). Many of our existing tickets improve batching heuristics or kernel matching independently; this ticket packages two tightly-coupled runtime changes: (1) an adaptive admission-surface optimizer that reshapes how prefill requests are admitted to the prefill queue based on instantaneous kernel-fit utility and tail risk, and (2) an attention-prefetch policy that proactively warms attention KV caches and selects kernel variants earlier in the prefill -> decode handoff to avoid decode-time stalls.

Goals:
- Reduce 95th/99th token latency for mixed short+long streams by 20–35% without lowering average throughput by more than 5%.
- Avoid any regression on 50th/75th latency and throughput SLOs.
- Provide observability hooks (per-request kernel choice, prefetch decision, reason code) for post-rollout regression detection.

Success metrics:
- 95th token latency reduction >= 20% on benchmark mix (70% short, 30% long).
- 99th latency reduction >= 15% on same benchmark.
- No >5% throughput drop on steady-state synthetic load.
- New trace fields available in Console for 100% of production requests after rollout.

Proposed design (high level):
1) Admission surface optimizer (ASO):
   - Compute a lightweight per-request "kernel-fit utility" score at admission using: model profile, sequence-length estimate, cached KV hit probability, and current kernel queue occupancy.
   - Use an admission policy that accepts requests to prefill slots that maximizes expected throughput while bounding expected tail-latency risk via a sliding-window quantile estimator.
   - The optimizer runs on the serving node's admission layer and assigns a reason code (e.g., accepted-fast-path, delayed-prefill, rejected-burst-backpressure) stored in request metadata.

2) Attention-prefetch policy (APP):
   - On prefill acceptance, make an early decision whether to prefetch KV blocks and select kernel variant (FP16 / Q4 / int8-ish) needed for decode.
   - Prefetch uses an LRU-weighted prefetch queue prioritized by predicted reuse (prefix similarity and session affinity) and by kernel candidate warm score.
   - Kernel variant selection is optimistic: for ambiguous cases select the lower-latency compatible variant; attach fallback plan to decode path in case mismatch discovered (transparent model fallback with metrics emitted).

Trade-offs and rationale:
- Prefetch increases GPU memory pressure; mitigation: conservative prefetch budget per-GPU and prefetch eviction by reuse score.
- Early kernel selection risks mismatch when downstream decode needs higher-precision; mitigation: always provide a fast fallback path and measure fallback rate (target <1%).
- Optimizer complexity vs benefit: keep kernel-fit utility computation O(1) and cache recent estimates to avoid admission CPU spikes.
comments: 2026-01-15 — Initial spike analysis attached (see attachments). Short/long mixture reproduces 2x 99th latency vs all-short baseline.
2026-01-27 — Prototype admission scoring landed in sandbox branch: github.com/redwood/runtime/pulls/432. Early microbench: 12% 95th improvement but prefetch memory pressure high on 4-GPU node.
2026-02-05 — Design review feedback from runtime-ops: add explicit per-tenant prefetch budgets and quota checks (will reuse Dedicated quota primitives).
2026-02-18 — Asha ran offline sim harness for 48h with mixed traffic; preliminary numbers: 22% 95th reduction, fallback rate 0.9% when optimistic kernel selection enabled.
2026-03-02 — Engineering review: flagging kernel-selection telemetry schema change needed (see attachments telemetry-rfc).
acceptance_criteria: Load test with mixed short/long whitebox traffic shows >=20% 95th latency improvement and <=5% throughput regression compared to baseline.
All production traces include admission_reason, kernel_variant_choice, and prefetch_decision fields.
Per-tenant prefetch budget enforcement enabled and can be toggled via console feature flag.
Fallback rate <1% on representative workloads or documented mitigation plan if higher.
implementation_steps: 1) Implement lightweight kernel-fit utility and incorporate into admission path (ENG sandbox branch).
2) Add prefetch queue with per-GPU budget and reuse-weighting, wire into prefill acceptance path.
3) Implement optimistic kernel-variant selection with attached fallback plan and telemetry emission.
4) Integrate per-tenant quota checks and console flag for prefetch budgets.
5) Run 72h A/B private cluster run, collect 50th/95th/99th token latencies, throughput, GPU memory metrics.
6) Rollout canary (10% traffic) -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback if 95th latency increases or fallback rate >2%.
